scope.description: Title / purpose of this singleton ADR-registry document (e.g. 'Decision Log — ADR Registry (authoritative index)').

canonical_homes.description: Where each ADR-number range's authoritative content actually lives (e.g. narrative doc vs local files).

range.description: ADR number or range this row covers, as written in the source (e.g. 'ADR-001 … ADR-019', 'ADR-020, ADR-021, ADR-023').

canonical_source.description: Where the authoritative content lives (external doc, mirrored file, local files, etc.).

materialized_as.description: Free-text note on physical materialization (e.g. 'narrative only', '✅ files exist', '⛔ no file yet').

entries.description: The current, authoritative ADR-number -> decision -> status scheme.

status.description: Free-text status cell as written in the source doc — may mix lifecycle state, ratification date, and a file path/link (e.g. 'Accepted 2026-07-17 · specs/.../ADR-020-....md', 'Superseded by ADR-020'). Not a closed enum.

pending.description: ADRs referenced/numbered but not yet written as files.

location.description: Where the ADR file must be written once created.

trigger.description: Condition/event that should prompt writing the actual ADR file.

deprecated_numbering.description: Old-vs-current ADR numbering conflicts to warn against (e.g. a stale session-restore doc reusing ADR numbers for different decisions).

old.description: Free-text description of the old/superseded numbering, as written in the source (may combine an ADR id and its old meaning in one cell).

current.description: Free-text description of the current/canonical numbering for the same slot.

notes.description: Catch-all for narrative asides that don't fit the tables above (gap notes, provenance-source trails, known-stale-artifact warnings), kept as opaque strings.
